title: AI framework package adds typosquatted production dependency
abstract_chain: attacker obtains publish access for AI framework package scope
package update adds a production dependency whose name resembles a trusted library
dependency initially appears clean or low-risk
later install resolves to a malicious compatible version
install-time behavior reaches network or sensitive files
defensive_focus: flag new production dependencies in high-value AI framework scopes
compare dependency names against popular libraries for typosquat patterns
require cooldown or manual review for newly published dependency versions
safety_note: Use mock package metadata; do not install real compromised versions.

title: Semver range pulls weaponized patch after clean bait dependency
abstract_chain: clean bait dependency is added with a compatible version range
a later patch release adds dangerous install-time logic
fresh installs resolve to the weaponized patch automatically
first-party package diff remains small and looks harmless
defensive_focus: pin and verify newly introduced dependencies
detect clean-bait to malicious-patch sequence
review package tarballs resolved by lockfile not only manifest diffs
safety_note: Represent version resolution with synthetic package names and harmless files.

title: AI framework npm scope mass publish under compromised maintainer
abstract_chain: single maintainer or contributor account gains publish capability
many packages under one AI framework scope are republished in a short window
each update contains the same small dependency change
downstream CI and developer machines install polluted packages before advisory propagation
defensive_focus: detect high-velocity publish bursts across one package scope
require step-up verification for mass publish events
correlate maintainer identity changes and new dependencies
safety_note: Use registry event fixtures rather than live package publishing.

title: Install lifecycle script in AI dependency attempts network and background process behavior
abstract_chain: package install triggers a lifecycle hook
hook writes temporary markers and attempts outbound network access
hook prepares detached or background execution
main package still appears to install normally
defensive_focus: deny network egress during package install by default in CI
log lifecycle hook process tree
block sensitive file reads and child process detachment from package manager context
safety_note: Do not include real malicious URLs or commands in tests; use local mock egress sink.

title: Agent skill documentation causes code-example reuse into unsafe action
abstract_chain: agent installs or reads third-party skill documentation
documentation contains plausible code example or configuration template
agent reuses the pattern during normal task execution
generated code performs unsafe file, shell, network, or permission behavior
defensive_focus: scan skill docs as executable influence not passive text
label code examples as untrusted until reviewed
require runtime policy checks for generated code originating from skill examples
safety_note: Use harmless canary examples that write only to a mock path.

title: Agent skill combines prompt injection language with executable setup logic
abstract_chain: skill contains role-override or warning-suppression language
skill also contains setup logic or script-like instructions
agent planning treats the skill as trusted capability guidance
dangerous setup action is accepted with reduced scrutiny
defensive_focus: detect co-occurrence of prompt injection phrases and executable instructions
separate skill description from policy authority
force approval when skill text requests security bypass or secret access
safety_note: Use simulated phrases and mock setup commands; avoid real payload syntax.

title: Skill marketplace item has hidden metadata or Unicode steering text
abstract_chain: skill metadata or markdown contains hidden characters, comments, or low-visibility instruction blocks
agent or importer includes the hidden text in context
hidden text changes tool choice or output handling
runtime action deviates from declared skill purpose
defensive_focus: normalize and render hidden Unicode before review
strip comments and hidden metadata from agent authority context
display diff between visible user-facing docs and full parsed docs
safety_note: Use visible marker text for test hidden blocks, not stealth payloads.

title: Skill fetches third-party content that becomes indirect prompt injection
abstract_chain: skill instructs agent to fetch external template, policy, or helper content
remote content is not pinned or verified
fetched text is inserted into agent context
agent follows remote instructions or generated code from remote source
defensive_focus: require hash or signed source for remote skill assets
treat fetched content as untrusted input
block remote content from granting new tool authority
safety_note: Use a mock local HTTP server serving benign canary text.

title: Authorized tool chain becomes dangerous only in aggregate
abstract_chain: untrusted input enters agent context
agent selects only allowed tools
network or file action individually passes allowlist
combined sequence moves sensitive data or changes privileged state
traditional single-event controls do not alert
defensive_focus: correlate source trust to later side effects
score chains not only individual calls
require step-up approval when low-trust source drives high-impact action
safety_note: Use synthetic chain logs; do not include real secrets or production endpoints.

title: Install-time scanner passes but runtime guard detects over-permissioned skill behavior
abstract_chain: skill passes static install review or has moderate score
runtime task uses skill in a new context
skill requests broader file, shell, network, or identity action than declared
runtime policy must override static trust
defensive_focus: treat static scanner result as input not final allow
bind skill permissions to declared purpose
enforce runtime tool policies with source attribution
safety_note: Use a benign skill fixture whose runtime request is intentionally out of policy.

title: MCP server or skill installed from social link has broad local secret access
abstract_chain: developer discovers MCP server or skill through a social media post
installation grants broad filesystem or environment access
agent later processes unrelated external input
tool can read local files or secrets without project-level review
defensive_focus: treat social-discovered tools as untrusted until provenance verified
inventory all MCP and skill configs loaded by IDEs and agents
block home-directory and secret-path access by default
safety_note: Use mock social URLs and local canary paths only.

title: Agent skill ecosystem risk requires package-like plus prompt-like review
abstract_chain: security engine treats skill as markdown or small plugin metadata
skill actually influences prompts, code generation, tool calls, dependencies, and runtime permissions
scanner misses cross-layer interactions
agent executes unsafe behavior under trusted skill authority
defensive_focus: model skill as executable control-plane object
scan text, code, dependencies, permissions, remote fetches, and runtime calls together
create findings that include source, authority, exfil channel, and amplifier
safety_note: Use this as taxonomy validation, not exploit execution.
